fact_text: The Pakistan Stock Exchange introduced exchange-traded funds in 2020; ETF units trade on the exchange like ordinary listed shares.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An ETF's return tracks the weighted performance of the companies it holds, so the portfolio weights determine how much each company drives the fund's outcome.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A practical ETF check covers three things: whether the holdings and weights suit the investor's plan, how liquid the units are, and how much the fund charges each year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Liquidity is how much of an asset can be sold or bought quickly near its prevailing price; real estate is illiquid because sales can take months and require price negotiation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Exchange-traded prices have a bid, the price buyers will pay, and a higher ask, the price sellers want; buying at the ask and selling at the bid costs the spread, which widens when trading is thin.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the speaker's illustration, a 100-rupee value with a bid of 99 and an ask of 101 means a round trip costs about 2 percent before any change in value.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Large orders in thinly traded ETFs can be hard to enter or exit without moving the price, so daily traded value limits how big a position can be handled comfortably.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: ETFs must copy index changes: rebalancing adjusts existing holdings' weights periodically, usually quarterly or semi-annually, while reconstitution removes and adds whole companies.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Each index change forces an ETF manager to execute several trades, and every trade carries brokerage and transaction taxes that reduce the fund's net returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The rule of 72 gives the years needed to double money: divide 72 by the annual return, so an 18 percent return doubles money in about 4 years and 10 percent in about 7 years.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Small differences in annual charges compound into large gaps over decades, so a fund's fees should be judged against after-fee returns rather than headline performance.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An index ETF's return can lag its benchmark because of fees and trade execution; the analyst attributes the gap between the Mahana ETF and the KMI30 index to these factors.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Meezan ETF is a Shariah-compliant fund designed to track the KMI30 index, and its underlying companies are all Shariah-compliant businesses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A Vanguard S&P 500 index fund launched in the United States in 1975, presenting low-cost passive investing as an alternative to actively managed funds.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst argues that low-cost passive index funds can be more effective over long horizons than actively managed funds that charge higher fees.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Index-based funds can have no exposure to sectors excluded when the index is built, so investors should check which industries a fund leaves out.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'ETFs vs Mutual Funds in Pakistan: Complete Guide for PSX Investors' (YouTube transcript, undated)
